entities.summary: A full-day traverse inside the Grand Canyon du Verdon, alternating cliffside trail, river-level passages, giant staircases and long tunnels.
entities.description: Walk the classic Maline-to-Point-Sublime direction through the depth of the Verdon rather than merely viewing the gorge from above. The route repeatedly changes character through steep descent, narrow ledges, the Mescla sector, Brèche Imbert stairs, river-level walking and the Trescaïre and Baou tunnels. The current mapped variant respects the temporary Couloir Samson rockfall closure by following RD23A and GR49 to Point Sublime.
entities.whyWorthwhile: France’s most complete canyon hiking experience: the route spends hours inside the limestone gorge and remains distinctive well beyond any single viewpoint.

values.accessPointNote: The route begins at Chalet de la Maline and ends at Point Sublime / the Visitor Center; the point-to-point day normally requires the reserved seasonal shuttle or a prearranged taxi.
values.bestSeason: Spring or autumn in dry stable weather; avoid July and August heat and winter rockfall conditions.
values.crowding: Very popular in summer; the official tourism office reports that traffic disperses after hikers enter the gorge, but shuttle capacity and narrow passages still reward advance planning.
values.exposure: Moderate to high in narrow cliffside sections and around steep stairs.
values.recommendedVariant: Chalet de la Maline to Point Sublime in the official recommended direction, using the current signed RD23A and GR49 detour after Couloir Samson while the direct exit remains closed.
specialHazards: temporary Couloir Samson rockfall closure and signed detour
values.technicality: Non-climbing mountain trail with long staircases, narrow passages, wet tunnels and rough rocky sections.

variants.description: The official direction through the full canyon from Chalet de la Maline to Point Sublime. This current variant follows the OSM Sentier Blanc-Martel relation to Couloir Samson, then uses the Park-directed RD23A and GR49 detour to the Visitor Center instead of the temporarily closed direct exit.

trailhead.name: Chalet de la Maline
trailhead.note: Exact first node of OSM hiking relation 5810021; normally reached by the morning Blanc-Martel shuttle from La Palud-sur-Verdon.

finish.name: Point Sublime Visitor Center
finish.note: Current detour finish on the visitor-center footway, close to the Point Sublime shuttle stop.

variants.accessNotes: This is a one-way traverse. Reserve the seasonal Blanc-Martel shuttle online or arrange a taxi; in 2026 the shuttle runs daily from 29 June to 13 September and on listed weekends/holidays in the spring and autumn operating periods.
variants.seasonalLimitations: Spring and autumn are preferred. Avoid July and August heat when possible, and winter because recurrent rockfall and adverse canyon conditions materially increase risk. Always recheck the live Park route notice before departure.
variants.waterAvailability: There is no dependable drinking-water refill in the canyon. Carry at least 2 litres per person, with more for heat, plus food and sun protection.
suitabilityConstraints: Not recommended for children under 8 or anyone sensitive to vertigo.
Dogs and mountain bikes are prohibited because of steep stairs and technical passages.
Requires fitness for a long rough day and enough pace margin to meet the return shuttle.
warnings: The direct Couloir Samson-to-Point-Sublime exit is temporarily closed after rockfall; follow RD23A and then GR49 as signed. The detour shares about 0.84 km of live RD23A with vehicle traffic and briefly uses D952, where a captured segment is tagged sidewalk=no; walk with care and follow all roadside directions.
Carry a headlamp for the long tunnels and expect slippery floors.
River level can rise quickly due to upstream dam operations; swimming is forbidden and riverbanks demand caution.
This OSM-derived Good Shit line is descriptive and non-navigation-grade; current signs and official closure notices are authoritative.

entities.summary: A free, long-season night route transforming Chartres’ cathedral, churches, bridges and civic buildings with light and sound.
entities.description: Chartres en Lumières is a distributed nocturnal attraction rather than a single projection show. Separate illuminated sites reward a two-to-four-hour self-guided walk through the cathedral quarter and riverside historic centre.
entities.whyWorthwhile: One of Europe’s strongest city-scale night environments: the architecture and public realm become a coherent visitor experience across an entire evening.
